title: Cellular and functional dissection of the octopaminergic and tyraminergic system in the Drosophila brain.
source_locator: Results 'ASM4/5 neurons acutely suppress aggression', para 2; Fig. 6B (image not available locally)
quote: Optogenetic activation of VL neurons and ASM1–3 neurons did not decrease aggression relative to genetic controls except OTA-SG05 (Figure 6B).
mapping_basis: Paper states the VL cluster comprises two descending subtypes, VL1 and VL2; VL1 matches the kit literature synonym OA-VL1 -> DNd02 (name differs by the 'OA-' prefix, so medium). Sibling 1 of 2 (alphabetical DNd02, DNd03).
stimulation: 655 nm red light, 10 ms pulses at 5 Hz, intensity 12μM/cm2 (as printed)
sensory_condition: socially isolated (6 d) male pairs in aggression arena, IR illumination
penetrance: aggression (lunge rate) not decreased relative to genetic controls
n_flies_note: number of pairs printed only in Fig. 6B (not available locally)
notes: Only outcome reported for VL lines is lunge rate (aggression); no leg or locomotion outcome stated for VL lines (Fig. 6D speed text mentions only OTA-SG08/SG10/SG40). The split-GAL4 line(s) used for 'VL neurons' are not named in the text and Fig. 6 is not available locally, so whether one line labels both VL1 and VL2 (multi_dn) is unknown. The two-type split follows the paper's statement that the VL cluster has two subtypes (VL1, VL2). Arguably no leg information; kept because the experiment exists and flies were video-recorded.

title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results 'Stationarity is necessary and sufficient to drive vibrations in males'; Fig. 3C-D; Fig. S4C; Table 1
quote: Conversely, inducing female walking by optogenetically activating the DNp28 neurons55,56 nearly abolished vibrations (Fig. 3C, D).
mapping_basis: Paper calls the neuron DNp28 but Table 1 gives the line as SS01587 = R11H10-p65.AD; VT033947-GAL4.DBD, which driver_lines.csv maps (Namiki 2018, two entries, identical hemidrivers) to DNp29; the DNp28 line in the kit is SS01056 (R17A04 x R24A03); mapped by driver line, conflict with the printed name.
stimulation: 625 nm red LED, 89 mW/cm2, 5 s on / 25 s off, 30 trials
sensory_condition: female courted by wild-type male in 44 mm chamber on paper over microphones; room light off
penetrance: female velocity rises from ~1 mm/s to ~12 mm/s during light (Fig. 3C trial average); not given per fly
notes: Walking inferred from body-centroid velocity tracking (no leg tracking), coded 'increased locomotion' per convention: all legs yes, confidence medium. Pre-stimulus female velocity is low (~1 mm/s), so this is largely initiation of walking rather than only a speed change. Walking direction not stated; forward_walking assumed from the paper's 'inducing female walking'/'acceleration'. Name/line conflict: printed name DNp28 vs kit line identity DNp29 for SS01587; adjudication may wish to check.

title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results 'Central song neurons drive song and vibration with complex dynamics'; Fig. 4B; Table 1
quote: The activation of the descending neurons pIP10 or pMP2 drove song but no vibrations.
mapping_basis: pIP10 is itself a MANC type name in type_list.csv (one type).
stimulation: 625 nm red LED, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 14 mW/cm2 in order, 5 s on / 115 s off, 15 trials
sensory_condition: solitary males in chamber on paper over microphones; room light off
penetrance: fraction of males singing = 1 (Fig. 4B, all intensities pooled); no vibrations
notes: Song (wing) is the only reported outcome; legs not described, so not_assessed per convention. The paper's own circuit model (pIP10/DNvib) is not a Pugliese-type score.

title: An optogenetics device with smartphone video capture to introduce neurotechnology and systems neuroscience to high school students.
source_locator: Fig 2A-B; Results 'Device validation–activating escape neurons'; S1 Movie (not downloaded)
quote: We found that only flies that expressed CsChrimson in the GF and had been fed retinal displayed takeoff behaviors (Fig 2B and S1 Movie).
mapping_basis: Paper writes 'GF (also known in the literature as DNp01)'; GF is a kit synonym mapping only to DNp01.
stimulation: 627 nm red LED, 0.16 mW/mm2 at the fly, single 300 ms pulse; flies fed all-trans-retinal
sensory_condition: tethered on tungsten wire, holding a small piece of Kimwipe; dark-recovered; filmed via smartphone through stereoscope
coordination_notes: middle leg extension, wing depression, flight initiation (Fig 2A)
penetrance: ~83% of flies escaped (Fig 2B bar); 0% in controls
notes: Paper calls the driver a 'highly specific genetic driver line GF-split-Gal4'. Single movement (takeoff) coded as no rhythm. 'male and female flies' used, so sex mixed. Escape scored by a non-blinded experimenter.

title: An optogenetics device with smartphone video capture to introduce neurotechnology and systems neuroscience to high school students.
source_locator: Fig 3A-B; Results 'Device validation–activating freezing neurons'; S2 Movie (not downloaded)
quote: We found that flies expressing CsChrimson in neurons labeled by this line displayed freezing behavior at a high probability
mapping_basis: Paper names DNp09 (Namiki nomenclature, line SS1540 from Namiki 2018); the kit marks the name DNp09 ambiguous (MANC DNp09 vs DNp71 via hemibrain) and SS01540 as AMBIGUOUS DNp09;DNp71; chose MANC DNp09 as the Namiki-named type, no anatomy given in the paper.
stimulation: 627 nm red LED, 0.16 mW/mm2 at the fly, single 300 ms pulse; flies fed all-trans-retinal
sensory_condition: tethered on tungsten wire without tarsal contact; Kimwipe given and removed to induce active leg movement; dark-recovered
other_cell_types: other (unidentified) neurons labelled by SS1540-split-Gal4, suggested by the paper to cause freezing
coordination_notes: complete interruption of appendage movement; freezing = >=120 ms absence of leg motion
penetrance: ~62% of retinal-fed flies froze (Fig 3B bar); ~20% of non-retinal-fed SS1540 flies; 0% wild-type controls
n_flies_note: 80 retinal-fed SS1540 x CsChr flies; 79 non-retinal; 24 per WT control
notes: The paper itself says freezing in this line may come from other labelled neurons rather than DNp09, and that DNp09 has been suggested to drive forward locomotion, which they did not observe (tethered, no tarsal contact). Freezing interrupts pre-existing leg movements (struggling/grooming) of tethered flies. Annotation by a non-blinded experimenter.
